messages.subject: Negative Binomial Formulation
parts:
Dear all,

I use the Negative Binomial to model distribution of counts. The way the NegBin is formulated in RStan isn't realy the same as in Wikipedia ... and I'm not strong enough to handle such troubles :-).
I modelled as follow:

Count[i] ~ NegBin( N[i], 1/f) 

where N[i] is the size of the sample ; and "f" is the frequency of occurence of the success.
But as you write an " \alpha -1" in the definition of the density function, should I write: "Count[i] ~ NegBin( N[i]+1, 1/mu)"?


Thank you

messages.author: 20758fda448fdbda
messages.subject: Re: Negative Binomial Formulation
parts:
There are two major ways the negative binomial is defined in the literature. One is the way followed by R, DeGroot, Wolfram, etc. and the other is the way followed by Gelman, Wikipedia, etc. Stan is following the Gelman parametrization (which makes sense as Dr. Gelman is one of the key people behind Stan) so (unless I made an error with the algebra) neg_binomial(alpha, beta) represents a distribution with mean (alpha / beta) and variance alpha * (1 + beta) / beta^2.

Does that help?

On 14-03-18 11:39 AM, Leon-Alph wrote:
Dear all,

I use the Negative Binomial to model distribution of counts. The way the NegBin is formulated in RStan isn't realy the same as in Wikipedia ... and I'm not strong enough to handle such troubles :-).
I modelled as follow:

Count[i] ~ NegBin( N[i], 1/f) 

where N[i] is the size of the sample ; and "f" is the frequency of occurence of the success.
But as you write an " \alpha -1" in the definition of the density function, should I write: "Count[i] ~ NegBin( N[i]+1, 1/mu)"?

Stan uses the parametrization of Bayesian Data Analysis book, comparing to wikipedia's definition you'll have (1-p)=beta/(beta+1) and r=alpha.

Is N[i] the number of failures until the experiment is stopped? Or is it the number of successes until the experiment is stopped. Both parametrizations ocorr in literature.

If it's the latter, then
Count[i] ~ NegBin( N[i], 1/f)  in your parametrization is
Count[i] ~ neg_binomial( N[i], f-1) in Stan parametrization

If it's the former, then
Count[i] ~ NegBin( N[i], 1/f)  in your parametrization is
Count[i] ~ neg_binomial( N[i], 1/(f-1)) in Stan parametrization

Note: this wasn't tested, so confirm that this calculations are correct in simple example before using them



Thank you
